claim: Balanced pursuit of exploration and exploitation is not reliably better than focus: the 2014 meta-analysis of 117 studies found ambidexterity effects weaker than either focus, and Clauss 2020 (N=150) and Ebben-Johnson (N=300) agree. Wenke 2021 (34 studies, 5,488 SMEs) agrees for small firms; Fourne 2019 and Junni 2013 point the other way or are conditional, so status stays contested.
agent_test: Arms at equal tokens: fixed 50/50 explore/exploit, explore-only, exploit-only, adaptive. Score on solved-rate.

claim: Founding finding: in 41 business units performance rose stepwise with ambidexterity (3.21, 3.74, 4.10, 4.60; F=18.11).
agent_test: Not directly testable; a and b read the same paper.

claim: The Gibson-Birkinshaw top-group advantage is fragile: with separate raters the top two groups were equal (4.11 vs 4.13).
agent_test: Use separate judges for process scores and for outcome in any agent test.

claim: Contextual ambidexterity depends on interacting context traits (stretch, discipline, support, trust); interaction F=5.41, p=.003, n=41.
agent_test: Background only.

claim: Balance and interaction help sales growth: He and Wong found interaction positive and imbalance negative in 206 firms.
agent_test: Vary the explore:exploit token ratio and look for an imbalance penalty.

claim: Which side to favour depends on environment: exploratory innovation pays in dynamic settings, exploitative in competitive ones (Jansen 2006, betas 0.15 and -0.23/0.19).
agent_test: Set the explore share by task novelty; compare to a fixed share at equal tokens.

claim: Formal structure hurts exploration and helps exploitation; informal connectedness helps both (Jansen 2006: centralisation -0.17, formalisation 0.18, connectedness 0.20/0.21).
agent_test: Tight rubric on the exploit stage, loose on the explore stage; compare to a uniform rubric.

claim: Resource level moderates which form pays: balance for constrained firms, combined magnitude for resource-rich firms (Cao 2009).
agent_test: Run balance vs high-both at small and large token budgets.

claim: Meta-analytic sizes disagree: Kula 2023 reports g=0.77 for ambidexterity and innovation performance, far above Mathias 2014; likely inflated by common-source survey data.
agent_test: None; a warning about survey effect sizes.

claim: Ambidexterity measures are rated by the same managers as performance, so same-source bias inflates reported links (r=.78 adaptability-performance; r=.75 subjective vs financial at firm level).
agent_test: Use objective outcomes in agent tests.

claim: LLMs do not explore well in-context: GPT-4 basic prompt had suffix failures in over 60% of runs; only chain of thought plus an external summary worked.
agent_test: Compare in-context exploration against scaffold-forced exploration (external counter or UCB score) at equal tokens.

claim: LLM multi-agent peer selection is myopic; an external UCB score cut inferior-peer lock-in from 50.0% to 0.0% (Qwen-7B) and beat in-context exploration on Math500 and GPQA. Gap search: the 50.0% to 0.0% figure was not found in the part of the paper read (v3 text, first 100k chars); breadth is across five named models in one paper, no independent replication.
agent_test: Replicate with another model family and a non-toy task.

claim: LLMs help explore large semantic action spaces by proposing candidates, but every tested LLM lost to linear regression at exploitation.
agent_test: Use the LLM to generate candidates and a cheap statistical rule to select.

claim: Evolutionary LLM search keeps improving with diverse sampling; pure hill climbing plateaus and random search is worst.
agent_test: Archive with novelty rejection vs greedy best-only at equal tokens.

claim: Topology of multi-agent LLM collaboration matters: mesh beat tree beat chain on average; chain suited software, tree suited creative writing (MacNet).
agent_test: Match structure to task type at equal tokens.

claim: Surveys of AI-enabled exploration in firms (N=245, beta 0.604) are self-report studies of human firms, not evidence on LLM scaffolds.
agent_test: None; do not cite as agent evidence.

claim: No direct test of structural vs contextual ambidexterity exists for LLM agents: arXiv has 22 hits for ambidexterity and one on AI in firms. Closest analogues are a strategy-agent plus generation-agent split (d08, no numbers) and equal-token single vs multi-agent tests (d14, d15), which favour the single agent.
agent_test: Build one: separate explorer and exploiter agents vs one agent alternating, at equal tokens.

claim: Structural separation helps balance exploration and exploitation in firms of all sizes, more so in high-technology settings, while service firms gain from avoiding it (Fourne 2019, 114 studies, 33,492 organisations; abstract only).
agent_test: Compare separate explorer and exploiter agents with one alternating agent at equal tokens, on separable-stage tasks and on interactive tasks.

claim: On objective archival data the share of exploration has an inverted-U link to financial performance, with the optimum shifting with industry R&D intensity (Uotila 2009, S&P 500; abstract only).
schema_part: explore share set by task novelty
agent_test: Sweep explore share at fixed tokens on tasks of known novelty; look for an interior optimum.

claim: At equal thinking-token budgets above 500 tokens, one LLM agent matched or beat planner, role, debate and ensemble multi-agent splits on multi-hop QA; a centralised multi-agent system lost by 28 points on average in a pre-registered agent-serving test, using 2.8 to 6.1 times the tokens.
schema_part: structure choice: one agent with stages over separate agents
agent_test: Keep one agent with staged modes as default; require a split to prove itself at equal tokens.

claim: The best explore versus exploit allocation of LLM calls depends on task and model capability: interior optima on some tasks, no depth gain for a weak model; adaptive bandit allocation beat fixed greedy, random and island protocols by 12.3% over 8 cells; best search width rises with budget in equation discovery.
schema_part: adaptive explore share rather than fixed
agent_test: Compare adaptive vs fixed explore share at small and large budgets; capability gate for small models.

claim: Frontier LLMs say they will explore but do not: in biochemical optimisation, stated exploration intent (about 92% of traces) had about zero correlation with realised novelty, and no configuration beat a mean statistical baseline; an explicit exploration instruction did not fix it.
schema_part: explore operator driven by scaffold, not by instruction
agent_test: Replace explore-by-instruction with an external novelty or uncertainty rule and measure realised novelty.

claim: Diversity controls in LLM evolutionary search (diverse init, island selection, migration) give small gains within one standard deviation on one task; island count was never ablated in any paper found; search strategies do not expand the quality-novelty frontier (Heuresis, 3,222 runs).
agent_test: Low priority; if built, ablate island count and init diversity with 10 or more seeds.
